clues: This town stands on a wide river in the south-west of its province. It rules its own self, apart from the county round it.
Summer day highs reach 30 here, and winter nights can fall to minus 20. Snow falls from October to April.
This town bears the name of a Mohawk chief and war lord. His folk moved here in the wake of a great war.
Folk call this the Telephone Town. The first phone was made here, at the home of the maker's father.
The most peopled first-folk reserve in the land lies just south of this town. Kin of its name-sake chief live there still.
